claims.text: Short-range order evolves with time near FCC/BCC interfaces in nanoscale high-entropy-alloy multilayers under sustained stress.
Interfacial SRO evolution intermittently pins dislocations.
Interfacial SRO evolution modulates slip across FCC/BCC interfaces.
The interface- and SRO-mediated process governs creep in nanoscale FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers.
This creep process maintains strength while preserving some deformation tolerance.
As-deposited nanoscale FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers can contain short-range chemical order.
Sustained loading at approximately 0.5–0.7 Tm promotes time-dependent plastic strain.
Interfacial SRO reconfiguration produces multi-stage creep and delays cross-interface slip.
Localized diffusion under steady loading rearranges SRO near multilayer interfaces.
SRO rearrangement creates barriers to dislocation glide.
Time-varying glide barriers cause transient creep resistance and staged plastic deformation.
The multilayer initially has high creep resistance that degrades as SRO evolves or is disrupted.
Early holding will show reduced creep rates, followed by more rapid deformation at longer hold times.
Briefly loaded baseline multilayer coatings exhibit negligible creep, limited dislocation activity, and limited interface evolution.
The proposed mechanism dominates when interfaces remain well defined and temperature provides sufficient mobility for dislocations and vacancy-driven processes.
Excessive interlayer diffusion or secondary-phase formation can obscure SRO-mediated effects.
Mechanical deformation can produce SRO whose extent depends on loading rate.
Chemical SRO can affect dislocation behavior, deformation microstructure, local plastic strain, and strength in multi-principal-element alloys.

contradictions.description: SRO evolution or rearrangement is said to create dislocation barriers and transient creep resistance, but SRO evolution is also predicted to degrade creep resistance. The hypothesis does not specify which type or stage of SRO evolution strengthens versus weakens the barrier.
